correctness.rationale: Finite étale duality leaves exactly the split and quadratic-field coalgebra forms. The split count is the verified \(21\)-table census modulo its \(C_2\) automorphism, giving \(13\), with \(6\) nonzero-entry orbits. For the nonsplit form, separability of \(\mathbb F_{q^2}/\mathbb F_q\) in every characteristic splits the coalgebra after base change; Galois descent is exactly the simultaneous swap on the same table set, yielding \(5\) fixed tables, \(3\) with no zero entry. The nonsplit coalgebra automorphism group is the quadratic Galois group, so distinct fixed tables remain nonisomorphic. Adding the two forms gives \(18\) and \(9\).

The final theorem crosses that boundary using separable étale descent and classifies the complete finite-field étale slice.

value.rationale: Two-dimensional étale coalgebras form a canonical structural slice with exactly two finite-field forms. Determining the complete product-class count on both forms, uniformly in \(q\), resolves the characteristic-two field-of-definition boundary left open by the recent characteristic-not-two classification. The result is a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice, and the separate \(18\)/\(9\) counts clarify the effect of the counit convention.
